name: Browderism
summary: Browderism is the line of the American Communist leader Earl Browder in 1943 to 1945: the wartime anti-fascist alliance, with the Soviet Union and big capital included, should continue into a long peace, and American socialists should accept the capitalist economy as the base of a national unity program. Browder dissolved the Communist Party into a non-partisan political association, urged cooperation between unions and employers, and backed national independence for colonial peoples. Moscow's disapproval led to its repudiation in 1945.
scope: The Teheran line of 1943 to 1945 as set out in Browder's Teheran: Our Path in War and Peace (1944) and Teheran and America, and as described by the Encyclopedia of the Great Plains and Encyclopedia.com, which tie the name Browderism to his wartime policy of class cooperation and the Communist Political Association. It excludes his earlier Comintern-era and Popular Front positions, his post-1946 views, and his opponents' use of the word for any compromise with capitalism.

class-collaboration.rationale: Chapters IX, X and XII make employers and workers partners in national unity, with labor and management on the same plane and cooperating to double purchasing power.

defeat-communism.rationale: Chapter IV holds that neither the capitalist nor the socialist side can be abolished by the other, so each must adapt to the other; the Soviet alliance is to last into the peace.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The Teheran perspective is a generation of peace between capitalist and socialist great powers and a postwar world kept stable by their cooperation, which rejects any inevitable capitalist road to great-power war.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Browder expects the present American system to deliver expanded production and employment after the war, but only if government and business raise mass purchasing power; he warns it is otherwise doomed.

avoid-permanent-military-alliances.rationale: He wants the Anglo-Soviet-American coalition, nucleus of the United Nations, to continue as a long-term alliance after victory.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: He argues the wartime alliance must be extended into the peace, the opposite of ending permanent alliances.

workers-own-party.rationale: Chapter XVI has the Communists dissolve their separate party, saying it no longer serves a practical purpose, and work as independents through the existing two-party system.

vanguard-party.rationale: Browder turned the party into a non-partisan political association; his scholarly biographer reads this as abandoning the Leninist vanguard role.

national-self-determination.rationale: He accepts unconditionally self-government and self-determination for Asian and African peoples, calls independence inevitable for India and Southeast Asia, and urges recognition of Puerto Rican nationhood.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: He calls the colonial system contrary to America's interest and incompatible with industrialization, and wants colonial administrations superseded by self-government with a schedule for self-determination.

delink-world-market.rationale: He wants Asia, Africa and Latin America industrialized through American credits and brought into the main stream of world trade, not cut off from it.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: His postwar plan for developing poor regions rests on large American investments, long-term credits and joint development corporations.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: He treats a vast expansion of foreign markets and world trade as an inescapable necessity for America, not a self-contained bloc.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: He hopes the United Nations as a centre of world collaboration can be continued and extended, and proposes an international body to administer African development.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: The sources record no position on colonial-era treaties.

unions-good.rationale: Chapter XII calls labor unions an indispensable feature of democracy and the means by which wage earners become active citizens.

collective-bargaining.rationale: He welcomes capitalist statements that old laissez-faire capitalism that rejected collective bargaining is gone, and puts unions and management on an equal plane negotiating wages.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Chapter XI proposes to raise the floor of the minimum wage in all industry as part of doubling mass purchasing power.

job-guarantee.rationale: He accepts a program in which business has the first chance at full employment and the government steps in to make good any gap, quoting that citizens will be employed by business or by government.

regulate-corporations.rationale: He calls for a minimum of government regulation to curb the anti-social and anti-national tendencies of big capital, while preferring its self-limitation.

ban-cartels.rationale: He dismisses trust-busting and abolishing cartels as chatter and says any such plank would have to be ceremonial, since it would throw the capitalists into the opposing camp.

widespread-small-property.rationale: He says breaking up concentrated capital is impossible and a pastime for chatterboxes, yet also says small business must be protected and given a chance to develop.

cut-welfare.rationale: He treats the whole gamut of social insurance and health and educational policy as productive investment in the working population.

night-watchman-state.rationale: He says government must take responsibility for creating markets and sustaining employment if private enterprise fails, far beyond defence and justice.

price-controls-fight-inflation.rationale: He faults Congress for rejecting Roosevelt's anti-inflation program and condemns Lewis for working against government price control.

worker-farmer-alliance.rationale: He names industrial labor and the farmers together as the working classes of the national coalition and wants business, labor and agriculture to cooperate.

democracy-best.rationale: Chapter XIII demands the unconditional right of the majority to rule together with the defence of minorities and the abolition of restrictions on the franchise.

property-franchise.rationale: He demands abolition of the poll tax and all other forms of restricting the franchise.

racial-franchise.rationale: He demands the abolition of Jim Crow and the securing of unconditional equal citizenship for Negro Americans, with the poll tax abolished.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: He demands abolition of Jim Crow in law and in the armed forces and calls segregation a weapon against national unity.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: He demands equal citizenship guaranteed by the Constitution for all, with minorities protected, and treats racial supremacy as Hitler's doctrine.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: He urges active measures against Jim Crow, the poll tax and discrimination in employment, praising the Fair Employment Practices Committee.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: He demands the outlawing of anti-Semitism and all forms of racial supremacy theory and practice.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: He calls hostility to Jews as a group a Nazi import and the stigma of a man acting for Hitler's program.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: He rejects the Attorney General's assumption that Communist-led and Nazi-led countries are equally enemies and defends the Soviet Union as an ally.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: He describes the Soviet Union as operating on a different system, socialism, and as a great power to be treated as an equal.

socialism-one-country.rationale: He treats Soviet socialism as a lasting partner in the postwar order, with peace between it and capitalist states, rather than one needing revolution elsewhere.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: He is a self-described convinced socialist who accepts capitalism for a long period and holds that Marxism remains the guide to America's problems.

smash-state-machine.rationale: He has Communists work through the existing electoral system and collaborate with the Roosevelt government instead of replacing the state.

direct-action.rationale: He has Communists give up separate partisan struggle and work through elections and existing parties to elect candidates.

gradual-change.rationale: He judges that the American people are ill-prepared for deep change and that postwar plans must start from existing institutions and proceed step by step.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Chapter XVII says an unprecedented, unorthodox policy is correct if it contributes to winning the war and a durable peace, and wrong if it fails.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: He presents American Communists as patriots who ask workers and the nation to unite for the national interest, and stresses American Marxism for American conditions.

party-own-road.rationale: The Comintern was dissolved in 1943 and Browder organized an American association; his biographer says he assumed he led an independent movement.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: He holds that labor must back its government's war effort to victory and calls the opposite policy defeatism.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: He wants an all-out war effort, with labor refraining from strikes until victory, and denounces defeatism.

armed-resistance-to-occupation.rationale: He praises the people's army of Yugoslavia and the Polish patriot army fighting Nazi occupation as a model of liberation.

non-intervention.rationale: He rejects the objection that urging China toward unity would be interference in its internal affairs, calling it a sophistical evasion, and says America must have a policy on its internal regime.

suppress-opposition.rationale: He condemns persecution of Communists for their opinions and defends minority rights, yet says the defeatist press and disruptive forces must be halted and repression of them is necessary.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: He says religious freedom and tolerance demand a respectful attitude toward all religious beliefs and the persons who hold them, which excludes a state campaign for atheism.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: He holds that persecution of people for their religion, Jews or Catholics, is the concern of all citizens and demands defeat of anti-Catholic trends.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: He opposes persecution on account of religion and treats religious freedom and tolerance as a principle to be respected.

restrict-conversion.rationale: He defends religious freedom and tolerance for all beliefs and opposes discrimination against any religious group.

religious-nation.rationale: He wants equal citizenship for Jews, Catholics and every religious minority, and calls anti-Semitism and anti-Catholicism threats to national unity.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: He calls hostility, discrimination and segregation against Jews a Nazi import and demands the outlawing of anti-Semitism.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: He praises the Fair Employment Practices Committee for breaking down obstacles to the employment of Negroes, Jews, Mexicans and other minorities and demands outlawing anti-Semitism and racial supremacy practice.
